First, we find ${f}^{′}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,k \\  & =({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+{e}^{t}\,j+({e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute ${f}^{′}(\pi )$ we substitute $t=\pi $ into the expression for ${f}^{′}(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =({e}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +{e}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )\,i+{e}^{\pi }\,j+({e}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -{e}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi )\,k \\  & =({e}^{\pi }\cdot 0+{e}^{\pi }\cdot (-1))\,i+{e}^{\pi }\,j+({e}^{\pi }\cdot (-1)-{e}^{\pi }\cdot 0)\,k \\  & =-{e}^{\pi }\,i+{e}^{\pi }\,j-{e}^{\pi }\,k\end{aligned}
$$
